segments.text: Arjun and Meera are both twenty-eight. Same job, same salary, same city: Bangalore.
segments.caption: Arjun and Meera are both 28. Same job, same salary, same city: Bangalore.

segments.text: And both their parents give them the same gift: twenty-five lakh rupees.
segments.caption: And both their parents give them the same gift: ₹25 lakh.

segments.text: One buys a flat. One rents.
segments.caption: One buys a flat. One rents.

segments.text: Twenty years later, the gap is more than one crore.
segments.caption: Twenty years later, the gap is more than ₹1 crore.

segments.text: But it almost went the other way.
segments.caption: But it almost went the other way.

segments.text: Arjun's father has one rule: rent is money thrown away.
segments.caption: Arjun's father has one rule: "Rent is money thrown away."

segments.text: So Arjun buys a ninety-lakh flat.
segments.caption: So Arjun buys a ₹90 lakh flat.

segments.text: His twenty-five lakh goes on the down payment, stamp duty and registration.
segments.caption: His ₹25 lakh goes on the down payment, stamp duty and registration.

segments.text: The rest is a home loan at eight and a half percent. His EMI: sixty-two thousand five hundred a month, for twenty years.
segments.caption: The rest is a home loan at 8.5%. His EMI: ₹62,500 a month, for 20 years.

segments.text: Meera rents a similar flat next door, for twenty-one thousand a month.
segments.caption: Meera rents a similar flat next door, for ₹21,000 a month.

segments.text: She puts her twenty-five lakh into an index fund.
segments.caption: She puts her ₹25 lakh into an index fund.

segments.text: And every month, she invests the difference between owning and renting: about forty-five thousand rupees.
segments.caption: And every month, she invests the difference between owning and renting: about ₹45,000.

segments.text: Her mother is not impressed.
segments.caption: Her mother is not impressed.

segments.text: For five years, the plan works.
segments.caption: For five years, the plan works.

segments.text: Her rent goes up every year, but her investments grow faster.
segments.caption: Her rent goes up every year, but her investments grow faster.

segments.text: By year five, Meera has seventy-eight lakh. Arjun's share of his flat: fifty-one.
segments.caption: By year 5, Meera has ₹78 lakh. Arjun's share of his flat: ₹51 lakh.

segments.text: Then, in year six, the market crashes thirty-five percent.
segments.caption: Then, in year 6, the market crashes 35%.

segments.text: Meera loses twenty-three lakh on paper. For the first time, Arjun is ahead.
segments.caption: Meera loses ₹23 lakh on paper. For the first time, Arjun is ahead.

segments.text: Her mother calls. Her friends are selling. Every instinct says: get out.
segments.caption: Her mother calls. Her friends are selling. Every instinct says: get out.

segments.text: Meera does nothing. She keeps investing, every single month.
segments.caption: Meera does nothing. She keeps investing, every single month.

segments.text: Fourteen years later, Arjun owns his flat outright. It's worth about two point four crore.
segments.caption: Fourteen years later, Arjun owns his flat outright. It's worth about ₹2.4 crore.

segments.text: Meera's portfolio: four point one crore.
segments.caption: Meera's portfolio: ₹4.1 crore.

segments.text: But here's what the spreadsheet doesn't show.
segments.caption: But here's what the spreadsheet doesn't show.

segments.text: If Meera had sold in that crash, and waited three years to feel safe again, she'd have ended with two point six crore.
segments.caption: If Meera had sold in that crash, and waited three years to feel safe again, she'd have ended with ₹2.6 crore.

segments.text: One panic would have cost her one and a half crore.
segments.caption: One panic would have cost her ₹1.5 crore.

segments.text: And if Bangalore prices had grown eight percent a year instead of five, Arjun would have won.
segments.caption: And if Bangalore prices had grown 8% a year instead of 5%, Arjun would have won.

segments.text: So renting doesn't beat buying. Discipline does.
segments.caption: So renting doesn't beat buying. Discipline does.

segments.text: Renting only wins if you invest the difference, every month, through every crash.
segments.caption: Renting only wins if you invest the difference, every month, through every crash.

segments.text: And Arjun? No landlord ever asked him to leave. That's worth something too.
segments.caption: And Arjun? No landlord ever asked him to leave. That's worth something too.
